root_cause.summary: src/spotify-api.js request() ended with `return res.json()` unconditionally. PUT /me/player/play returns 204 No Content (empty body) → res.json() throws SyntaxError → the throw propagated to prime()'s catch in src/player.js (notifyError("prime-failed")) even though Spotify had already received the play command and started the track. Consequences: the «No se pudo preparar la canción» toast (round 2) / persistent «No se pudo conectar el reproductor» banner (round 1), prime() returned false → ensurePaused() never ran → the track kept playing with no pause, and the game's Play button was dead (if (!round.primed) return). Rounds 1 and 2 symptoms shared this single cause.
root_cause.fix: request() success path: 204/205 → return null; otherwise read text; empty text → null; else JSON.parse. A successful play PUT now resolves instead of throwing. Other behaviors (401 refresh+retry, 429/QUOTA backoff, 403 handling) unchanged.

fixes.A_root_cause: src/spotify-api.js — 204/205/empty-body success path returns null (no throw).
fixes.B_silence_guard: src/player.js — state.clipActive (false initial); playClip() sets true, stop() sets false; player_state_changed listener pauses when !state.clipActive && st && st.paused === false. Defense in depth: the device is never left playing outside a clip regardless of missed/late pauses.
fixes.C_play_never_dead: clip-game.js + year-game.js Play handlers — if not primed: one fresh-prime retry (round.priming = ctx.player.prime(round.track.uri); round.primed = await round.priming); still not primed → ui.toast("El reproductor todavía no está listo. Probá de nuevo.", "error") and return; if primed → play as usual. Existing in-flight-prime await kept.
